terra.problem: The middle-manager joke makes the LORD’s role as keeper the target of workplace humor.
The coffee-break joke applies workplace humor to the LORD’s guarding and mentions a food or drink outside the permitted exceptions.
The passage does not say nobody is hunting for the vineyard.
The explanation is generic and ends by merely pointing back to the verse.
The final line makes the treatment of the thorns and briers unconditional, but the LORD speaks of what He would do if they confronted Him.
Saying the LORD faces the thorns and briers turns the conditional confrontation into an event.
The text says Israel fills the world with fruit, not that the plant itself grows big or moves beyond one field.
The calves do not have the place to themselves: the next verse says women come and use the dry limbs for kindling.
The explanation is flat and largely repeats that the reason is stated, without adding clarity or warmth.
The claim that nobody gets lost in a crowd goes beyond the promise that Israelites will be gathered one by one.
One by one does not say they are gathered in single file or that each person is on their own.
The passage says the exiles in Egypt come forth; it does not say nobody at all is left in Egypt.
Nobody stays behind is broader than the text’s statement that the exiles in Egypt come forth.
Saying they leave Egypt to worship assigns a purpose to their departure that the text does not state.
